source.snippet: I work as a freelance software engineer on a long-term contract for a small 20-30 people company. Company is pushing for AI everywhere. Recently I had a call with team lead / head of engineering / CTO. We were talking about how AI generated 1200 lines of code for a project I am working on. And how I am supposed to review it. She recommended me to do a high level code review and not go line-by-line. It's fine with me but what if there's a bug that causes damage? I need to protect myself legally.

problem_statement: Freelance software contractors are being asked to sign off on large volumes of AI-generated code without the time or tooling to review it properly, creating unresolved legal liability and job-security risk they currently have no structured way to document or mitigate.
target_segment: Freelance and independent software contractors working on contracts with AI-forward SMB clients
notes: Clear paying-buyer context: a freelancer on a paid long-term contract facing a real professional risk. The gap is a product that helps contractors document their review scope, generate audit trails, and attach coverage disclaimers when accepting AI-assisted codebases. Adjacent to code-review tooling (paid market: Codacy, SonarQube). Willingness to pay is implied by the professional stakes (contract value, liability). Signal strength 3: concrete scenario, business context, but single data point.
